passage: L1.3: "Feature selection on the entire dataset results in using information about which feature performs well" (Results, 'Toward a solution: A taxonomy of data leakage', PMC10499856; sentence cut by the fetch tool).
faulty: The 20 features with the largest absolute Pearson correlation with y are chosen on all 100 rows; then 5-fold cross-validation (fold = i mod 5) of ridge (lambda 10, standardised, intercept) on the 20 chosen features; pooled R-squared = 1 - SSE/SST >= 0.10.
fixed: In each fold the 20 features are chosen from the 80 training rows only; ridge fitted on them predicts the 20 held-out rows; pooled R-squared >= 0.10.
estimand: Faulty: R-squared of a model whose features were chosen with the held-out outcomes. Fixed: out-of-sample R-squared of the whole pipeline (choice plus ridge) for new samples.
model_family: Top-20 filter by absolute Pearson correlation, then ridge (lambda 10, standardised). Source names none.
sizes_note: Source states none. 100 x 500 = 50,000 values: imaging-style small-n many-features regime; the check is 5 correlation sweeps and 5 small ridge fits. Dependence on feature count: not stated.
exploited_structure: Many candidate features relative to samples, so features chosen for their association with the outcome include chance associations that the held-out rows share.
